title: Volunteer page: choose a layout
question: Three layouts for the Volunteer page, written for surgeons, anesthesia providers, nurses and other clinicians first, with non-medical roles after. Pick one, add a note to steer it, or re-roll.

options.label: A colleague's letter
options.thesis: A volunteer clinician writes to colleagues about serving, with the roles listed beside the letter.
options.viewport: Title and lede across the top; the letter in large italic serif at left with its sample tag and signature; the roles and the Volunteer button in a column at right.
options.risk: Until a real volunteer writes the letter, the centerpiece is a labeled sample.

options.label: Vision first
options.thesis: The mission card's Vision opens the page, so clinicians read why before what.
options.viewport: Centered: Our Vision, the cobalt dash and the vision statement; under it the page title, a short lede and two buttons; the roles begin below.
options.risk: The first screen is the ministry's words; the practical details start lower down.

options.label: The way in
options.thesis: Joining is five numbered steps, so a clinician sees exactly what's involved before they reach out.
options.viewport: Title, lede and button at left; at right five numbered steps with brushed rules: tell us about you, a conversation, credentialing, orientation, your first surgery day.
options.risk: Close to the home page's process section, so it can read as a repeat.
